Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified extract of the foreign corporate general partner's registry of directors and beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Global Affairs Canada or foreign competent authority)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / status certificate for the non-resident general partner entity
Notarized beneficial ownership and source-of-funds declaration for all limited partners and the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if executed outside Canada; otherwise recognized under provincial evidence rules

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original NUANS name search report for the proposed limited partnership name
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: ISED – Corporations Canada / authorised service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Not required - issued by the Canadian federal registry

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners, and authorised signatories against Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions list, United Nations Security Council sanctions, Canadian Criminal Code terrorist entity lists, and OFAC SDN list for USD clearing; enhanced due diligence required for foreign politically exposed persons in accordance with PCMLTFA and FINTRAC's Client Identification and Verification guidance; source-of-funds verification for all retainer wires; ongoing transaction monitoring for B2B cross-border payments.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada – Name Search and NUANS Report portal (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada); provincial registries for extra-provincial limited partnership registration (e.g., Ontario Companies and Personal Property Security Branch).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must include a distinctive element and a legal element ('Limited', 'L.P.' or 'société en commandite' for Quebec). The name may be English, French, or bilingual; foreign words must be transliterated into Latin characters and accompanied by a translation or explanation. Names must not imply a prohibited activity or closely resemble any existing Canadian or extra-provincial registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal, Corporations Canada issues a non-approval letter with reasons. The applicant may file a written reconsideration request to the Director of Corporations Canada (ISED) within 30 days, supported by revised submissions. Alternatively, applicant may submit a new NUANS report with a different distinctive element. If the refusal is upheld, judicial review in the Federal Court of Canada remains available. For provincial LP filings, a similar administrative appeal may be made to the provincial registry director within the statutory deadline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is generally permissible for maintaining a registered office address provided that a physical service address and a named registered agent in the province are maintained, and books and records remain accessible for inspection. However, for an executive search and headhunting agency receiving retainer fees and requiring commercial substance under Canadian tax and AML rules, a dedicated physical office or established coworking presence is strongly advised to avoid reassessment of tax residence and to satisfy provincial record-keeping and licensing expectations.

Escrow safeguards and retainer payment compliance review for cross-border executive search B2B wires

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 5(1), 16 (for corporate general partner); applicable provincial Limited Partnerships Act (e.g., Ontario Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.6, s. 4) for the limited partnership's declaration of registration; CA_FED denotes federal CRA tax registration, while the LP registry is provincial.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada) for the CBCA general partner; provincial Companies/Registry office (e.g., Ontario Companies Office) for the LP; Canada Revenue Agency for federal business/tax account registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation/Compliance for the general partner; Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form A) filed with the provincial registry; CRA Business Number Form RC1 for federal tax identification.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a limited partnership; partners determine capital contributions in the Limited Partnership Agreement. No federal escrow account requirement; any escrow arrangement is purely contractual agreement between partners and a Canadian Schedule I bank.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Limited Partnership Agreement of [CA_LP] be, and it is hereby, adopted as the governing charter; that the officers of the General Partner be, and they are, authorized to execute and file the Declaration of Limited Partnership with the provincial registry; that the registered office of the Partnership be established at [address]; that the initial capital subscription of [amount] CAD be approved; that [Name] be appointed Chief Executive Officer and [Name] Chief Financial Officer of the General Partner; and that the CFO/Secretary be authorized to open bank accounts, sign business documents, obtain the CRA business number, and apply for all municipal and occupational licences.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: NUANS System via Corporations Canada or provincial registry online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search to ensure proposed limited partnership name is distinctive in the jurisdiction. Reserve the name with the provincial registry for 90 days and, if necessary, incorporate a CBCA corporate general partner using Corporations Canada's Online Filing Centre.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report
Name reservation application/form
Consent to use name, if any prior nameholder consent is required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name is rejected for lack of distinctiveness, file a revised name or provide written consent of the existing nameholder within 15 days; otherwise extend the reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute Limited Partnership Agreement and general partner incorporation documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel or notary public (preformation preparation; no government filing at this stage)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Limited Partnership Agreement setting out capital contributions, profit/loss allocations, management rights of the general partner, and dissolution terms. All partners execute the LPA; the corporate general partner files its articles under the CBCA with Corporations Canada.
required_dossiers: Draft Limited Partnership Agreement
Certificates/identification of all partners and officers
CBCA articles of incorporation or articles of amendment for the corporate general partner
Executed consent/resolution of the corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any governing document is ambiguous or rejected by the registry, file a conforming amendment to the LPA or corporate articles; cure notarial defects by re-execution before a notary public.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Declaration and obtain Certificate of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Companies Office / Registry (online filing portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed Declaration of Limited Partnership and the required fee through the provincial registry. State the registered office address and the corporate general partner's name and jurisdiction. Upon approval, receive the Certificate of Limited Partnership.
required_dossiers: Signed Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form A)
LP name reservation certificate
Registered office address (lease or authorization letter)
Certified copy of the corporate general partner's certificate of status
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction notice, file a declaration of amendment within 21 days; if the initial declaration is defective, withdraw and refile to avoid deemed general-partner liability during the defect period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal tax and business number registration with CRA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration (CRA Business Registration Online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the CRA business registration questionnaire online to obtain a 9-digit Business Number (BN) for the limited partnership. Open or elect GST/HST, payroll, or import/export accounts as needed. The LP uses its BN for CRA filings, including T5013 partnership information returns.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Limited Partnership
Partners' legal names, addresses, and tax identification numbers
SIN or CRA BN of individual partners / corporate BN of corporate partners
Bank account details for direct deposit or remittance set-up
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA flags an eligibility or address discrepancy, provide the Certificate of Limited Partnership and partner affidavit via the CRA corporate business line or My Business Account to correct the record within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal business licence and occupational clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Business Licensing Centre; provincial Employment Standards / Workplace Safety authority (e.g., Ontario Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development; WSIB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business licence for the executive-search office using the LP name and registered office address. If not exempt under provincial law, apply for a provincial employment agency licence. Coordinate fire safety inspection, building occupancy clearance, and WSIB account registration for employees.
required_dossiers: Municipal business licence application
Employment agency licence application (if applicable and not exempt)
Commercial lease or proof of registered office address
Fire safety and occupancy inspection certificate
Workplace Safety and Insurance Board (WSIB) registration record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licensing authority issues a deficiency notice, supply amended floor plans or compliance undertaking within 10 business days; use an expedited inspection request for critical business-continuity matters.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Business Licensing Office and provincial Employment Standards Branch (where not exempt for executive search placement activities)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business License / Employment Agency Licence (for headhunting and executive-search placement services, as statutorily required)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (federal) / provincial environmental ministry (e.g., Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category A 'Service Industry'; no designated project under the federal Impact Assessment Act; no environmental impact assessment required for office-based headhunting operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for a dry office environment; zero process wastewater, zero VOCs, municipal solid-waste diversion and recycling by-law compliance; electric/electronic equipment disposal per provincial electronics EPR regulation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under applicable Fire Code with annual inspection; structural/occupancy compliance certificate from local building authority; occupational health and safety clearance under the Canada Labour Code or provincial occupational health and safety act; Workplace Safety and Insurance Board (WSIB) coverage established for employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada via My Business Account portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities and non-resident Limited Partnerships carrying on business in Canada or making taxable supplies in Canada must obtain a federal Business Number (BN) and, if registering for GST/HST, a separate GST/HST account number. Apply online through CRA Business Registration Online, or file Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) for Canadian partnerships; non-resident applicants typically file Form RC459 (Request for a Business Number and GST/HST Registration for Non-Residents). CRA may require a security deposit under Excise Tax Act section 296 where the non-resident has no Canadian establishment. The LP itself is a taxable 'person' for GST/HST purposes and must provide its partnership declaration and constituent/partner identification; each partner derives income through the partnership for income tax purposes and is subject to the applicable Part I income tax rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible; Canada applies a flow-through/partnership model under subsection 96(1) of the Income Tax Act; the Limited Partnership is not taxable at entity level for income tax, but is treated as a registrant/person for GST/HST purposes. Scope: federal residency-based taxation, with non-resident partners subject to Part XIII withholding on certain distributions and Part I tax on Canadian-source business income attributable to the partnership.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No 'check-the-box' election analogous to the United States exists in Canadian federal tax law. The LP is statutorily classified as a partnership. Relevant statutory elections include: (i) partnership fiscal-period election under subsection 249.1(1) of the Income Tax Act; (ii) GST/HST partnership election where one partner is appointed as registrar/representative on Form RC1 and accountable for the partnership's net tax; (iii) joint partnership filing elections for income allocation under Form T5013 Summary filing rules; and (iv) hybrid mismatch limitation mechanisms under Canada's anti-hybrid legislation which can recharacterize payments arising from dual-entity or branch mismatches for Canadian tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) / Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) administered federally by the Canada Revenue Agency; provincial sales tax regimes apply separately in non-HST provinces.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: 30,000 CAD in annual Canadian taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated supplies) triggers mandatory GST/HST registration for a small supplier; no threshold applies for non-residents seeking voluntary registration, and mandatory registration may arise earlier for non-residents who solicit orders in Canada or supply advisory/headhunting services performed in Canada.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time e-invoicing or fiscal clearance/stamping regime exists at the federal level. CRA accepts electronic invoices (PDF, XML, EDI) provided the records are accurate, auditable, and retained under the Electronic Records and Electronic Books requirements (RC4058). Canada participates in Peppol interoperability by adopting pan-Canadian standards; however, issuance of invoices remains a commercial practice rather than a statutory real-time filing condition. GST/HST returns must be filed separately via CRA e-services, including GST/HST NETFILE or represent-a-client portals.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Executive search/headhunting services supplied to a non-resident client are generally zero-rated under section 1 of Part V, Schedule VI, Excise Tax Act when the service is supplied to a non-resident individual/entity and is not supplied in connection with real property situated in Canada, tangible personal property situated in Canada, or a service rendered wholly within Canada on tangible personal property. Additionally, the supply must not be 'made in Canada' under section 142 of the Excise Tax Act. Eligibility requires the supplier to maintain records demonstrating the non-resident status of the recipient, the nature/place of the service, and the fact that the service was exported/consumed outside Canada. Where services are performed both in and outside Canada, a reasonable apportionment based on time/location of service activities is required.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice describing the executive search service and identifying the non-resident purchaser
Executed contract/retainer agreement with the non-resident client
Proof of non-resident status of the recipient (e.g., foreign tax registration or business address evidence)
Customs Export Declaration only if physical goods are exported; for services, a detailed service statement and engagement letter
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill where the service is bundled with export logistics
Inward Remittance Certificate or wire transfer/transaction record showing receipt of payment from outside Canada
T5013/Income tax records or TP-approved transfer-pricing documentation confirming cross-border service performance
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may deny zero-rating and reassess net tax on the supply if the exporter fails to produce corroborative export documentation within the 180-day repatriation/receipt window. Penalties include: (i) unreported/understated GST/HST penalties under Excise Tax Act section 280 (5% plus 1% per month up to a maximum); (ii) false statement penalties under section 285.1 of up to CAD 25,000 and 10% of the aggregate of taxes sought to be evaded; (iii) full retrospective clawback with interest at prescribed rates; and (iv) criminal prosecution for tax evasion involving fines of up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment. For artificial schemes lacking economic substance, general anti-avoidance rules under Income Tax Act section 245 may also apply to deny partnership-level tax benefits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), with prudential oversight of banks and foreign exchange matters distributed between OSFI (Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions) and FINTRAC for AML/CTF supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. Canada maintains no general foreign exchange controls or restrictions on the repatriation of profits, dividends, interest, or capital. A non-resident limited partner may remit Canadian dollar funds in and out freely, subject only to ordinary tax withholding obligations on Canadian-source income and anti-money laundering reporting thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or forced conversion requirements apply to export receipts or any other foreign currency proceeds. Canadian residents and non-residents may maintain foreign currency bank accounts and remit funds abroad without Central Bank approval. Export transactions are reported for statistical purposes only.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. Internationally licensed digital EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer, and Airwallex may offer Canadian dollar settlement accounts and B2B payment rails that are operationally viable for retainer collection and cross-border disbursements. However, they are not Schedule I chartered banks and typically do not hold deposits in Canada. Legal constraints include: (i) no CDIC deposit insurance; (ii) separate corporate onboarding may still require the underlying LP to open a bank account at a regulated Canadian financial institution; (iii) EMI KYC procedures may be more flexible but do not replace statutory obligations under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not universally mandated but is strongly preferred by tier-1 Canadian banks for non-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners. Most Schedule I banks require at least one signatory with physical presence or an in-person/video verification interview. Remote opening is available but usually limited to residents of comparable AML jurisdictions (US, UK, EU, Australia) and requires enhanced due diligence, notarized certified copies, and a Canadian registered office address. The general partners and limited partners of the Canadian LP should be prepared for virtual KYC interviews if they are already banked in FATF-compliant jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident general partner or limited partner with no Canadian presence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate certificates of incumbency, constitutional documents, register of directors and shareholders, passport copies, proof of address, fund source statements from the investing entity's bank, negative news screening report, and a written explanation of the LP's commercial purpose confirming that the executive search and headhunting activity is a genuine operational business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from an offshore jurisdiction or from a third-party payer not named as a partner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed capital contribution agreement, duly notarized resolution of the general partner, bank statement showing the source account and transaction narrative, tax transparency declarations for the LP, and a sworn declaration confirming that the injected funds do not originate from proceeds of crime or unreported economic activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected wire frequency or invoice payments from low-correlation counterparties (headhunting clients)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete client engagement contracts, retainer invoices, dated payment schedules, proof of placement deliverables, and a clear mapping of each inbound wire to a named fee-paying client and corresponding commission/refund obligations under ISIC 7830 executive search scope.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership complexity of a limited partnership structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full org chart covering general partner, limited partners, and ultimate beneficial owners; a written authorization naming all persons with more than 10% ownership interest; certified passports; tax identification letters; and a FINTRAC-compliant politically exposed persons (PEP) screening result for each officer and partner.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital contributions should be routed via SWIFT MT103/TT from the foreign partner's bank account to the LP's Canadian-dollar or US-dollar account held at a Schedule I bank. Remittance instructions should include the remitter's identity, the reference 'Capital Contribution – [LP Name]', and the specific purpose code required by the remitting bank (e.g., '1300 – Equity Capital' or '7020 – Other Domestic Equity'). The receiving Canadian bank will verify source-of-funds documentation under PCMLTFA and may request a capital contribution statement or notarized partnership resolution. No Bank of Canada approval is required, but transactions exceeding CAD 10,000 trigger FINTRAC large cash transaction reporting, and all wire transfers are reportable under FINTRAC electronic funds transfer rules.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For operating expenditures and trade settlements, the LP should use the SWIFT MT103 wire rail for direct transfers and retainer fee settlements to international recruiters or service providers. Commercial letters of credit (LC) are permissible but unnecessary for low-risk executive search collections. CAD-to-foreign-currency disbursements are executed by the commercial bank at prevailing market rates; no Canadian exchange control license is required. The LP may also leverage Wise B2B API for small-value cross-border retainer payments, but settlement between partner and client should remain on the SWIFT rail for audit trail completeness.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX forwards for CAD/USD and CAD/EUR hedging of committed retainer revenue
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only through OSFI-regulated Canadian banks or approved foreign bank branches if the counterparty does not require physical CAD delivery
Cross-currency swaps for long-term matched funding of non-resident partner distributions
FX options (call/put) for treasury risk management on nominal amounts, provided the LP does not engage in speculative derivatives trading inconsistent with its headhunting scope

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (with T5013 slips and summary)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 following each calendar year-end; non-calendar fiscal periods are subject to the CRA information-return deadline applicable to that fiscal period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 20 per day per return, minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 2,500; continued failure may trigger CRA enforcement action and mandatory audited financial statement requests

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Provincial annual return / annual declaration for the Limited Partnership register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial corporate and business registry where the LP is registered (e.g., Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, B.C. Registry, or Alberta Corporate Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the limited partnership's provincial registration (provincial rules vary by registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fee and potential administrative strike-off from the provincial register; after strike-off, the LP cannot lawfully carry on business and limited partners may lose limited-liability protection for post-strike-off obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Executive search / headhunting recruiter licence annual renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial employment standards regulator (e.g., Ontario Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development, or other provincial licensing authority where the agency operates)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of licence grant or prescribed provincial renewal date; in Ontario, renewal must be completed before expiry of the current licence year under the Employment Standards Act, 2000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating without a renewed recruiter licence may result in administrative penalties, cease-and-desist orders, fines, loss of entitlement to collect placement fees, and potential prosecution

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Canadian limited partnership is not subject to a federal statutory audit merely because of its size. A mandatory independent audit is triggered if the LP is a reporting issuer under provincial securities legislation, a registered investment fund, or if the Canada Revenue Agency, a lender, or the partnership agreement requires audited financial statements. For a federally incorporated CBCA corporation, an audit can also be requisitioned by shareholders holding at least 5% of the voting shares; distributing corporations are required to appoint an auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE (Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) for private entities. A Canadian limited partnership may generally adopt either IFRS or ASPE, except where a reporting issuer or regulator mandates IFRS; CRA accepts either framework for tax compliance.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Canada does not currently impose a federal UBO confirmation protocol specifically on limited partnerships. If the LP is a federally incorporated entity under the CBCA framework, an individuals-with-significant-control (ISC) register must be confirmed annually alongside the CBCA annual return. For an ordinary Canadian limited partnership, the annual provincial declaration/return must remain accurate with respect to general and limited partners; internal registers must be updated on any transfer of partnership interests, and provincial registry amendments must be filed as applicable. Executive-search and headhunting LPs should also perform annual KYC / beneficial-ownership reviews consistent with Canadian AML obligations.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Copies of declaration of limited partnership and all amendments
Financial records supporting the T5013 Partnership Information Return

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300-1,200 per annum for a Canadian registered office and registered agent service, depending on province and service provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000-18,000 per annum for an executive-search/headhunting limited partnership when an audit is required by a lender, investor, regulator, or partnership agreement

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% (federal general corporate rate); combined federal-provincial headline rate approx. 26.5%; CCPC active-business rate 9% federal on first CA$500,000 of taxable income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sector-specific tax holiday for ISIC 7830. General preferences: Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) Small Business Deduction (9% federal rate), investment tax credits (ITCs), accelerated capital cost allowance (CCA) and Scientific Research & Experimental Development (SR&ED) credits, none of which confer a territorial exemption; the LP is fiscally transparent and the rate applies at the partner level.
